SOURCE_EXT = {".go", ".rs", ".ts", ".mod", ".cpp", ".java", ".py", ".yml", ".yaml",
              ".json", ".sh", ".jar", ".lua", ".conf", ".cfg", ".ini", ".toml", ".xml"}
# Other file extensions: weak.
OTHER_EXT = {".js", ".md", ".txt", ".test", ".spec", ".php", ".c", ".h", ".html", ".css"}
# Closing quote + colon of a JSON key (the colon token variants).
KEY_CLOSE = {'":', "':", '\\":'}
# Format letters that follow a "%" sign.
FORMAT_LETTERS = set("dsvqfxtc")
# The text right before a colon is a plain identifier (possibly with a leading space).
IDENT = re.compile(r"\s?[A-Za-z_]\w*")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (stack, document) where stack holds, per open "{", the last ',' or ';' seen in it.
    stack, doc = carry if carry else ([], None)
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:
        stack = []
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]

    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 else ""

    if tok in SOURCE_EXT or tok == "py":  # bare "py" after "__." or "*." is the same extension
        value = 0.9
    elif tok in OTHER_EXT:
        value = 0.3
    elif tok in KEY_CLOSE:
        value = 0.8
    elif tok == ":" and stack and stack[-1] != ";" and IDENT.fullmatch(prev):
        # key: value inside an object literal; deeper objects fire more.
        value = 0.4 if len(stack) == 1 else 0.6
    elif tok == "EOF":
        value = 2.0
    elif tok in FORMAT_LETTERS and prev.strip() == "%":
        value = 1.3
    elif tok == "··":
        value = 2.8
    else:
        value = 0.0

    stack = list(stack)
    for ch in tok:
        if ch == "{":
            stack.append("")
        elif ch == "}":
            if stack:
                stack.pop()
        elif ch in ",;" and stack:
            stack[-1] = ch
    return (stack, doc), value

"""Approximate a signal for the head of an English noun compound.

Look up adjacent words and established noun phrases in WordNet. Compounds
about objects, food and activities get the largest positive contributions;
place names get less. Noun modifiers and a few broad noun domains provide
weaker cues. These dictionary rules miss many collocations and wordpieces.
A short text tail is carried across tokens, but never across documents.
"""
import re
from functools import lru_cache
import regex
import wordnet

READS = ()

# Grammatical words should not be mistaken for dictionary senses of letters,
# chemical elements, units, or numbers.
FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''a an the this that these those i you he she it we they
me him her us them my your his its our their mine yours hers ours theirs
myself yourself himself herself itself ourselves yourselves themselves
am is are was were be being been do does did have has had having
can could may might must shall should will would ought
and or but nor so yet if then than though although because while whether
as at by for from in into of off on onto out over to under up upon with
about above after against along among around before behind below beneath
beside between beyond despite down during except inside near outside since
through throughout toward towards until via within without
not no yes all any each either every few many more most much neither
other several some such both only own same another what which who whom
whose where when why how there here once twice zero one two three four
five six seven eight nine ten'''.split())

DOMAIN_WEIGHTS = {
    'sport': 0.0733,
    'school': 0.077,
    'building': 0.0445,
}

COMPOUND_WEIGHTS = {
    'artifact': 0.2832,
    'food': 0.2418,
    'group': 0.1105,
    'person': 0.0879,
    'act': 0.1854,
    'communication': 0.076,
    'location': -0.0865,
}

MODIFIER_WEIGHTS = {
    'artifact': 0.0295,
    'food': 0.0732,
    'act': 0.0393,
}

HEAD_WEIGHTS = {
    'act': 0.0408,
    'artifact': 0.0441,
    'food': 0.0471,
    'group': 0.0318,
    'location': -0.0308,
}

BIAS = -0.0003
FIRST = -0.1311
HAN = 0.0390
KANA = -0.0281
NOUN_PAIR = 0.0191
DICTIONARY_COMPOUND = 0.0215
DICTIONARY_NOUN_PAIR = 0.0878
HYPHENATED = 0.0332


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def senses(word):
    if not word or word in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return frozenset(), frozenset()
    return wordnet.parts_of_speech(word), wordnet.categories(word)


def category_score(categories, weights):
    return sum(weight for name, weight in weights.items()
               if 'noun.' + name in categories)


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def token_score(token):
    value = BIAS
    if regex.search(r'\p{Script=Han}', token):
        value += HAN
    if regex.search(r'[\p{Hiragana}\p{Katakana}]', token):
        value += KANA
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if re.fullmatch('[a-z]+', word) and word not in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value += sum(weight for kind, weight in DOMAIN_WEIGHTS.items()
                     if wordnet.is_a(word, kind))
    return value


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    first = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    tail = '' if first else carry[1]
    tail = (tail + token)[-100:]
    text = tail.lower()
    value = token_score(token) + (FIRST if first else 0.0)

    # Work with words assembled so far, not just tokenizer fragments.
    match = re.search(
        r"([a-z]+(?:[-'][a-z]+)*)[ \t]+([a-z]+(?:[-'][a-z]+)*)$",
        text,
    )
    if match:
        modifier, head = match.groups()
        left_pos, left_categories = senses(modifier)
        right_pos, right_categories = senses(head)
        if 'noun' in right_pos:
            value += category_score(left_categories, MODIFIER_WEIGHTS)
            if 'noun' in left_pos:
                value += NOUN_PAIR
                value += category_score(right_categories, HEAD_WEIGHTS)

        phrase_pos, phrase_categories = senses(modifier + ' ' + head)
        if 'noun' in phrase_pos:
            value += DICTIONARY_COMPOUND
            value += category_score(phrase_categories, COMPOUND_WEIGHTS)
            if 'noun' in left_pos:
                value += DICTIONARY_NOUN_PAIR

    if re.search(r'[a-z]-[a-z]+$', text):
        value += HYPHENATED
    return (doc, tail), float(value)

"""Component layers.1.mlp.down_proj:310: a word-piece detector for "mun"-family stems.

What it responds to. The component is silent on nearly all text. It goes negative on the
word pieces that spell a few stems, and only there:
  * mun-: municipal, municipality, munitions, Munich, remuneration (and Russian муни-)
  * immun-: immune, immunity, immunoblot, immunoprecipitation (strongest on the piece
    "immun" itself and the piece right after it)
  * comun- / commun-: comunione, comunidade, communist, commune, communication, community
    (whole-word "community" and "communication" are only weakly negative)
  * lumin-: electroluminescent, written "electrolum|ines|cent", where the "ines" piece fires
  * huamn: the name piece "n" after "Huam" (about -1.8)
It is only mildly sensitive to the letters around the stem; it is about the stem spelled
across word pieces, not about the meaning of the whole word.

How the program works. It rebuilds the current word from the token strings (letters only,
lowercased), keeps the lengths of the last two pieces, and checks the stems in priority
order. A stem sets the prediction only if it ends inside the current piece, or, for stems
marked reach 2, inside the piece before it. The first matching stem wins; otherwise the
prediction is 0. Document boundaries reset the state, and the carry holds the state.

Values are the mean activations seen on training text, so this is a conceptual approximation:
it gets the stem family's sign and rough size, not every token.
"""

READS = ()

# (stem, predicted activation, reach), checked in order; reach 1: the stem must end in the
# current piece, reach 2: in the current piece or the one before it.
STEMS = [
    ("lumines", -5.0, 1),  # electroluminescent: "electrolum|ines|cent"
    ("муни", -4.4, 1),     # Russian муниципальный
    ("immun", -3.0, 2),    # immune, immunity, immunoblot, immunoprecipitation
    ("comun", -3.0, 2),    # comun-, comune, comunidad, comunicación
    ("commun", -1.8, 2),   # commun-: community, communication (weak as whole words)
    ("muni", -1.2, 2),     # muni-, municipal, munitions
    ("mun", -2.6, 2),      # mun-, remun-, Munich
    ("huamn", -1.8, 1),    # the name piece "n" after "Huam"
]


def _trailing_letters(text):
    i = len(text)
    while i > 0 and text[i - 1].isalpha():
        i -= 1
    return text[i:]


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, word so far, length of last piece, length of the piece before it)
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        word, last, before = "", 0, 0
    else:
        _, word, last, before = carry

    if tok.isalpha():                  # a letters-only piece continues the current word
        word, before, last = word + tok, last, len(tok)
    else:
        tail = _trailing_letters(tok)
        if tail:                       # e.g. " immun": a new word starts inside this piece
            word, before, last = tail, 0, len(tail)
        else:                          # punctuation, digits, spaces: no word now
            word, before, last = "", 0, 0

    cutoff = len(word) - last - before
    value = 0.0
    for stem, act, reach in STEMS:
        k = word.rfind(stem)
        end = k + len(stem)
        if k >= 0 and end > (cutoff if reach == 2 else len(word) - last):
            value = act
            break
    return (doc, word, last, before), value

"""A conservative spelling rule, not a semantic classifier.

Track the current word fragment. Look for p/f, then vowels and liquids r/l,
then an ending supplied by this token. M/f/y cues are negative; k/ng/g/w
cues are positive. Distinguish boundary-crossing and new p/f cues, and
reduce common whole-word matches using English word frequency.

Only Latin, Greek and Cyrillic spelling is transliterated. Reset at document
boundaries, with a small initial baseline and an initial 'def' adjustment.
This captures a broad spelling preference, not individual subword responses.
"""
import re
import unicodedata
from functools import lru_cache
from anyascii import anyascii
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency
READS = ()

# Ending, intervening-letter shape, location of the p/f cue -> response.
SCORES = {
    ('m', 'liquid', 'cross'): -0.89,
    ('m', 'liquid', 'embedded'): -0.56,
    ('m', 'e/o', 'cross'): -0.13,
    ('m', 'other', 'cross'): -0.34,
    ('f', 'liquid', 'cross'): -0.32,
    ('y', 'other', 'cross'): -0.48,
    ('k', 'liquid', 'cross'): 1.16,
    ('k', 'liquid', 'whole'): 0.87,
    ('k', 'e/o', 'cross'): 0.43,
    ('k', 'other', 'cross'): 0.14,
    ('k', 'other', 'embedded'): 0.12,
    ('ng', 'liquid', 'cross'): 0.63,
    ('ng', 'e/o', 'cross'): 0.16,
    ('g', 'liquid', 'cross'): 0.12,
    ('w', 'liquid', 'cross'): 0.25,
}
SUFFIX = (r'(?:s|es|ed|ing|er|ers|le|les|[aeiouy]|[aeiou]s|'
          r'ent[os]?|ents|ento|enta|ily)?$')
PATTERNS = []
for ending in ('m', 'f', 'y', 'k', 'ng', 'g', 'w'):
    consonant = {'k': r'(?:ck|nk|qu|k)', 'f': r'(?:ph|f)',
                 'w': r'(?:ough|ow|w)'}.get(ending, ending)
    gap = (r'[aeiouyrlhpfg]{0,7}' if ending == 'm'
           else r'[aeiouyrlhpf]{0,7}')
    pattern = re.compile(
        r'(?=([pf](' + gap + r')(' + consonant + r')(' + SUFFIX + r')))')
    PATTERNS.append((ending, pattern))

@lru_cache(maxsize=65536)
def letters(raw):
    # Transliterate alphabets, not Han characters into pinyin lookalikes.
    for char in raw:
        if ord(char) > 127 and char.isalpha():
            name = unicodedata.name(char, '')
            if not any(s in name for s in ('LATIN', 'GREEK', 'CYRILLIC')):
                return ''
    return anyascii(raw).lower()

@lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
def rarity(word):
    return max(0.0, min(1.0, (5 - zipf_frequency(word, 'en')) / 2))

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    start = carry is None or carry[0] != doc
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    s = letters(raw)
    prior = '' if start else carry[1]
    continued = bool(prior and re.match('[a-z]', s))
    old = prior if continued else ''
    text, boundary = old + s, len(old)
    cues = {}
    for ending, pattern in PATTERNS:
        for match in pattern.finditer(text):
            gap = match[2]
            if match.end(3) <= boundary or not any(c in 'aeiouy' for c in gap):
                continue
            if any(c in 'rl' for c in gap) and not gap.endswith(('i', 'u')):
                shape = 'liquid'
            else:
                shape = 'e/o' if any(c in 'eo' for c in gap) else 'other'
            if match.start(1) < boundary:
                kind, strength = 'cross', 1.0
            elif continued:
                kind, strength = 'embedded', float(bool(re.search('[pf]', old)))
            else:
                kind, strength = 'whole', rarity(s.strip())
            # An m preceded within this token by no r/l is a weaker cue.
            head = text[boundary:match.start(3)]
            if ending == 'm' and head and not any(c in 'rl' for c in head):
                strength *= 0.15
            cues[ending, shape, kind] = strength
    value = (0.09 if start else 0.0)
    value += sum(SCORES.get(key, 0.0) * x for key, x in cues.items())
    if start and raw == 'def':
        value = 3.6
    tail = re.search('[a-z]+$', text)
    return (doc, tail[0][-24:] if tail else ''), float(value)

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:311, a sparse word-piece feature.

It is quiet on most tokens. It fires on a word-continuation piece (a token with no
leading space, such as "ank" in "plank") when the piece before it is a short fragment
starting with "p" or "f" (pl, p, pe, ph, par, pre, fl, fr, ...). Its sign depends on the
word being spelled out:
  * positive for concrete English words built on pl-/p-/f- onsets: plank, plough,
    pong, peck, flock, fork, pork, flank, plow;
  * negative for French-looking or formal words built on par-/pre-/per-: parlement,
    parfait (-ement), preformed, parmi.

Only those word pieces are predicted; every other position predicts 0. The word lists
are the part a person can read; they are hand-picked from the rows we examined.
"""

READS = ()

# Continuation pieces that come out positive after a p-/f- fragment.
POSITIVE_PIECES = {"ank", "ong", "ough", "ow", "ows", "ck", "k", "rag", "ork", "locks", "anks"}
# Continuation pieces that come out negative after a p-/f- fragment.
NEGATIVE_PIECES = {"lement", "ement", "formed", "form", "former", "mi", "ett", "fer"}
SCALE = 1.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix.token_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    piece = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    before = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower()
    # A continuation piece: letters, no leading space.
    if not piece[:1].isalpha() or piece[:1] == " ":
        return carry, 0.0
    if before[:1] not in ("p", "f") or not before.isalpha():
        return carry, 0.0
    word = piece.lower()
    if word in POSITIVE_PIECES:
        return carry, SCALE
    if word in NEGATIVE_PIECES:
        return carry, -SCALE
    return carry, 0.0

"""Iberian word-fragment spelling, rather than a token lookup table.

Completed words supply a decaying Spanish/Portuguese/Catalan estimate,
using public word frequencies. In that context, short consonant-ending fragments
(especially es-, des-, ex- and vowel-initial fragments) give positive values;
ch/ll spellings and indefinites give negative values. Common whole
words and long fragments weaken some of these rules. Part of a fragment's
response persists into the next token of the same word. This approximation
omits the component's many smaller, word-specific responses.
"""
import math
import re
from functools import lru_cache
from wordfreq import zipf_frequency

READS = ()
LANGUAGES = ('es', 'pt', 'ca', 'en', 'fr', 'it', 'de', 'nl')
INDEFINITE = frozenset('un una uno unos unas um uma uns umas'.split())
PRONOUNS = frozenset('''yo tú usted ustedes ello ella ellos ellas
nós você vocês'''.split())


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def language_profile(word):
    return tuple(zipf_frequency(word, lang) for lang in LANGUAGES)


@lru_cache(maxsize=50000)
def spelling_response(token):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if not word.isalpha():
        return 0.0
    # Visible word starts strengthen the spelling rules.
    boundary = 1.0 if token.startswith(' ') or token[:1].isupper() else 0.5
    latin = float(word.isascii())
    initial = boundary * latin
    short = math.exp(-max(0, len(word) - 4) / 2)
    frequency = max(zipf_frequency(word, 'es'), zipf_frequency(word, 'pt'))
    incomplete = max(0.1, 1 - 0.25 * max(0, frequency - 4))
    ends_obstruent = word[-1] in 'bcdfgkpqtvxz'
    return (
        -0.73 * initial * bool(re.match(r'^es[^aeiou]+$', word))
        + 4.056 * initial * word.startswith('es')
        * (word[-1] not in 'aeiou') * short * incomplete
        + 0.534 * initial * (word[0] in 'aeiou')
        * ends_obstruent * (len(word) <= 4)
        + 0.518 * initial * word.endswith('f')
        + 0.369 * initial * bool(re.match(r'^en[bcdfgpqtvxz]+$', word))
        + 1.357 * initial * short
        * (bool(re.match(r'^ex[^aeiou]*$', word)) or word.startswith('extra'))
        + 1.898 * initial * short
        * bool(re.match(r'^des[^aeiou]*$', word))
        - 2.161 * ('ch' in word) * short * incomplete
        - 1.272 * ('ll' in word) * short * incomplete
        - 0.464 * (word in INDEFINITE)
        - 0.365 * (word in PRONOUNS)
        - 0.707 * (word.endswith('ch') or word.endswith('ll'))
        * min(1.0, len(word) / 4)
        + 1.122 * boundary * (word in ('in', 'im'))
    )


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        scores = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
        word, previous = '', 0.0
    else:
        _, scores, word, previous = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    text = ' ' if token.startswith('<|') else token
    for char in text:
        if char.isalpha():
            word = (word + char)[-50:]
        elif word:
            profile = language_profile(word.lower())
            mean = sum(profile) / len(profile)
            scores = tuple(0.93 * old + new - mean
                           for old, new in zip(scores, profile))
            word = ''
    margin = max(scores[:3]) - max(scores[3:]) - 6
    gate = 1 / (1 + math.exp(-max(-40, min(40, margin))))
    current = gate * spelling_response(token)
    continuation = bool(token) and token[0].isalpha()
    value = current + 0.25 * previous * continuation
    return (document, scores, word, current), float(value)

"""Layer 1, MLP neuron 313 (the component reads this neuron almost alone).

It fires on the first piece of a Spanish or Portuguese word that the tokenizer has split
into several pieces, when that piece is a Latin-root word start such as "esc" (escenario,
escuchar), "espec" (especies), "Est" (Estudio, Establecer), "Desc" (Descripción), "seg"
(seguida), "contr", "ampl", "oc", "ap". Read alone these pieces are not words, and the
neuron is strongly positive on them in training text. Almost everything else is near zero.

The program predicts a fixed activation for each such piece. The values are about half the
typical activation seen in training text, which scored better on held-out rows because the
neuron is only strongly active on these pieces in some contexts. Other tokens predict 0.
"""

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:314 — a weak, mostly-silent "modifier word" detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
  * Almost every token gets 0. The component is switched on only on a small minority of
    positions, and its strong responses are negative.
  * The strongest negative responses are on a content word (a noun, adjective or verb, not a
    function word) that sits early in a document, or inside a phrase, where a longer
    multi-word term is likely to continue: "law [enforcement]", "political [economy]",
    "Used [scrap] wood", "the [main] lake". Its output direction, when negative, boosts
    next-token candidates such as "Enforcement", "Defense", "Management", "Council", i.e. the
    head noun that tends to finish such a term.
  * The first token of each document gets a small positive value.

The numbers are the class means measured on 512 training rows; the program is a lookup over
these few readable classes, not a fit to individual tokens. Its variance explained is small,
because most of the variance sits in rare, context-specific large negatives that surface
word features cannot predict.

Main program: `step` runs once per token and tracks the position within the current
document (the carry resets at each document boundary, as the model's attention does).
"""

READS = ()

# Common function words: determiners, prepositions, conjunctions, pronouns, auxiliaries.
FUNCTION_WORDS = frozenset(
    """a an the of and or but nor to in on at by for with from as into onto over under
    about between through during before after than then so if that this these those which
    who whom what when where while there here also not no is are was were be been being
    it its he she they we you i his her their our my your me him them us do does did have
    has had will would can could should may might must shall""".split()
)


def is_content_word(token: str) -> bool:
    """A word token (leading space, letters only) that is not a function word."""
    word = token.strip()
    return token.startswith(" ") and word.isalpha() and word.lower() not in FUNCTION_WORDS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != document:
        position = 0  # first token of a new document (or of the row)
    else:
        position = carry[1] + 1
    carry = (document, position)

    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if position == 0:
        return carry, 0.1  # document start: small positive
    if not is_content_word(token):
        return carry, 0.0  # punctuation, digits, function words: silent
    if position <= 3:
        return carry, -0.13  # content word opening a document: strongly negative on average
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip()
    if not previous or previous.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS or previous.isalpha():
        return carry, -0.02  # content word after a function word or another word: mildly negative
    return carry, 0.0

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:315 -- the "ig" spelling detector.

What it does: this component fires on the letters "i" + "g" inside a word, when they
sit in a short word piece (a token of at most 4 letters, letters only), as in the
middle of a longer word:
  "Or|igen|es", "cor|rig|ida", "Bord|igh|era", "Cal|ig|ula", "ob|ige", "prod|igi|osa".
Strength:
  - "ig" followed by a vowel ("igen", "ige", "iga", "iger"): strongest, about 2.
  - "ig" in other short pieces ("ig", "ign", "igt", "igh", "rig", "dig"): about 1.
  - a "g" sound (g, Cyrillic г or ж) that starts a piece right after a piece ending in
    i, y or и: the same "ig" split across a token boundary, e.g. "intri|g", "Ty|g|ve",
    "интри|г": about 2.
  - a little extra when the piece continues a word that started in the previous token.
Ordinary English words with a short "ig" ("big", "high", "sign", "fig", "wig", ...)
are excluded: they are whole words, not "ig" fragments, and the component is quiet on them.
Longer words that merely contain "ig" ("significant", "design", "highly") are
excluded by the length rule.
At the first token of each document it dips slightly negative.

Units are the component's own activation (about -1 to 10; typical hit about 2).
"""

READS = ()

FIRST_TOKEN_DIP = -0.37   # first token of a document
IG_VOWEL = 2.0            # "ig" followed by a vowel: igen, ige, iga, iger
IG_OTHER = 1.0            # other "ig" pieces
G_SOUND_AFTER_I = 2.0     # piece starts with g / г / ж after an i, y or и ending
CONTINUES_WORD = 0.4      # extra when the piece continues a word
MAX_PIECE_LEN = 4         # longer pieces are whole words, not fragments
ENGLISH = {"big", "dig", "fig", "high", "pig", "sig", "sigh", "sign", "wig", "nigh", "ight", "eig"}
VOWELS = ("a", "e", "i", "o", "u")
G_SOUNDS = ("g", "г", "ж")
I_ENDINGS = ("i", "y", "и")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    if len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]:
        return None, FIRST_TOKEN_DIP
    raw = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    piece = raw.strip().lower()
    value = 0.0
    if piece.isalpha() and len(piece) <= MAX_PIECE_LEN and piece not in ENGLISH:
        i = piece.find("ig")

            value = IG_VOWEL if after in VOWELS else IG_OTHER
        elif piece[:1] in G_SOUNDS and prev.strip().lower()[-1:] in I_ENDINGS:
            if not raw[:1].isspace():
                value = G_SOUND_AFTER_I
        if value and prev.isalpha() and not prev[:1].isspace():
            value += CONTINUES_WORD
    return None, value

are strongly negative. The colon of an opening 'Title:' field is negative.
Opening digits get a small negative value increasing with digit magnitude;
tildes and the end-of-text marker get positive values. Identical repeats
retain the opening response. Later text gets a near-zero baseline; most
weaker, word-specific variation is deliberately not modeled.
"""

    '.\n': 1.83,
    '.\n\n': 1.34,
    ':\n': 1.31,
    ':\n\n': 1.09,
    ';\n': 0.83,
    ',\n': 0.95,
    ',\n\n': 0.98,
    '?\n': 0.97,
    '?\n\n': 0.91,
    '!\n': 0.90,
    '。\n': 1.18,
    '”\n\n': 1.18,
    '(\n': 0.57,
    ']\n': 1.10,
    '_\n': 1.03,
    ' *\n': 0.88,

    '-\n': 1.25,

    '\r\n': 1.79,
    '\n\n': 1.06,
    ' \n\n': 1.33,

"""layers.1.mlp.down_proj:316 — the first token of each document.

This component almost only acts at the very first token of a document (a packed
row restarts at each <|endoftext|> boundary, and attention never crosses one).
There the first token has no context, so its value depends only on the token itself:

- If the first token is a line break that closes a sentence or line of prose
  (".\\n", "?\\n\\n", ":\\n", "。\\n", ...), the component fires strongly (about +1.1).
- A bare line break or a line break after code punctuation (");\\n", "}\\n") fires
  weakly (about +0.5 to +0.6).
- A first token that is a word is mildly negative: capitalised words about -0.18,
  lowercase words -0.12, digits -0.17, other punctuation about -0.07.
- Every other position is about 0.

the model's output; the word-start negatives help the activation fit.
"""

READS = ()
PROSE_END = set(".!?。:;")
CODE = set("();{}[]\"'/")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc_start = prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if not doc_start:
        return carry, 0.0
    body = s.strip()
    if "\n" in s:
        if body[-1:] in PROSE_END:
            return carry, 1.1
        if any(ch in CODE for ch in body):
            return carry, 0.5
        return carry, 0.6
    if not body:
        return carry, -0.15
    if body[0].isupper():
        return carry, -0.18
    if body[0].isalpha():
        return carry, -0.12
    if body[0].isdigit():
        return carry, -0.17
    return carry, -0.07
